Write the workhorse counting feature and justify its normaliser from the
model rather than from convenience.
cards.reading:
The coefficient of variation of CSI amplitude: its standard deviation
divided by its mean, over a window.
cards.title: The counting feature

cards.explanation:
It follows from mass conservation under the HOMOGENEOUS-VELOCITY
assumption — everyone in an infinitesimal volume shares one mean velocity
— and it is the first-order LWR scalar conservation law. As a kinematic
identity it is exact. The thesis's contribution here is a documented
negative: imposed as a training-time regulariser it does NOT beat generic
smoothing on indoor geometry. A mismatched-closure ablation is what
settled it — a physically correct closure, a constant closure and an
ANTI-PHYSICAL closure gave identical high-density error, while plain
smoothing beat all three. A conservation term whose benefit survives
replacing the conservation law with its opposite is not acting as physics.
What survives is the density field as the estimation TARGET.

fields.meaning: crowd density field, people per square metre
bulk velocity field
pedestrian flux
local rate of density change

figures.caption: The whole content of the conservation law in one picture: no sources, no sinks. It is exact as a bookkeeping identity — which is precisely why it turned out to add nothing when used as a training penalty.

nodes.label:
a patch of floor
density ρ
ρ rises only if more comes in than goes out — nobody appears from nowhere

cards.question:
Write the continuity equation for a pedestrian continuum, name the
assumption that closes it, and state what this thesis did with it.
cards.reading:
Density at a point changes only through net flux divergence — no sources,
no sinks.
cards.title: The conservation law

cards.explanation:
Without a closure the continuity equation holds two unknown fields, ρ and
v, and cannot be integrated forward. The fundamental diagram resolves the
underdetermination by making speed a single-valued function of density.
Two things to be exact about. First, the free-flow value is 1.34 m/s — the
1.5 to 1.6 m/s figures in speed-prediction papers are congested-diagram
asymptotes, and quoting one as v₀ mixes two quantities. Second, the closure
is the only component the thesis treats as portable-and-refittable; the
eikonal direction field, obstacle geometry, corridor widths and exit
boundary conditions also change between venues and must be re-specified
separately.

fields.meaning: mean walking speed at density ρ (m/s)
free-flow desired speed (m/s)
jam density (ped/m²), where speed reaches zero
shape parameter of the Weidmann closure

figures.caption: Speed falls monotonically; flux is concave and peaks near 2 ped/m². Past capacity, more density means LESS throughput.

cards.question:
Write the Weidmann closure, and say why the continuum model cannot be
integrated without something of this shape.
cards.reading:
Walking speed falls from the free-flow value towards standstill as density
rises to the jam density.
cards.title: The fundamental diagram

cards.explanation:
The whole point is what this DOES NOT support. The exponent varies with
building materials, furniture and obstruction; multipath swings RSSI by
tens of decibels over small displacements; and bodies at 2.4 GHz absorb
and reflect in ways that depend on posture and orientation. A single
instantaneous reading is therefore a poor proxy for distance. The thesis
treats BLE RSSI as a COARSE RANGE BRACKET — enough to associate an
advertisement with a spatial zone and anchor a count — and never as a
ranging signal. Its own Fresnel-geometry analysis bounds this further: a
metre-grade BLE position may gate which link's sensitive region a body
occupies, and can never predict per-zone phase.

fields.meaning: transmitter–receiver distance
reference distance (commonly 1 m)
path-loss exponent — 2 in free space, above 4 when cluttered
zero-mean Gaussian shadowing term

figures.caption: The exponent is not a universal constant — it doubles between free space and a cluttered room, so it needs per-environment calibration.

cards.question:
Write the log-distance path-loss model and say what it is good for in this
architecture — and what it is not.
cards.reading:
Received level falls logarithmically with distance, at a rate set by the
path-loss exponent, plus a random shadowing term.
cards.title: The BLE range primitive

cards.explanation:
Read naively this is a heuristic. Read correctly it is the KALMAN GAIN
TRAJECTORY of a recursive Bayesian filter over a slowly-drifting
calibration state: BLE supplies a rare low-variance measurement of the
count, CSI a frequent higher-variance one whose calibration drifts, and
the optimal estimator's gain does exactly this. That reading is Pillar 3,
and it unifies two mechanisms the thesis first developed separately —
fusion is the filter's gain, and the recalibration trigger is a sequential
change-point rule on the filter's innovation. Note what the simulation
actually showed: a naive CONSTANT blend is dominated. The complementarity
is in TIME, not in density — an earlier density-axis formulation of this
claim was retired.

fields.meaning: elapsed time since the last calibration anchor
staleness time constant of the deployment
confidence weight on the anchor versus the CSI estimate

figures.caption: Fresh anchor: the absolute reference dominates. Stale anchor: the continuous relative sensor does. The switch tracks the lower envelope of the two error curves.
figures.x_label: Δt — time since the last anchor (units of τ)

cards.question:
Write the fusion weight, and say what it really is in the state-space
reading.
cards.reading:
The weight given to the device-count anchor decays exponentially with the
time since that anchor was taken.
cards.title: Pillar 3 — the staleness switch

cards.explanation:
This is the formal spine of the flagship result. Cross-environment
counting is ONE partial-pooling model: a shared crowd-to-signal link with
per-environment parameters nested under a hardware group. The curve's
concavity is the prediction — recovery versus anchor count rises steeply
then flattens — and the measured leave-one-environment-out result matches
it. Four mathematically independent LABEL-FREE alternatives were run under
pre-registered kill lines and all lost to two anchors, for a reason
domain-adaptation theory names in advance: the dominant error is a
session-structural offset that is not identifiable from the unlabelled
target marginal. No label-free objective can remove it. A local labelled
reference can.

fields.meaning: number of labelled anchors in the new environment
prior strength — how many anchors the population is worth
estimate from the local anchors alone
population-level estimate pooled across environments

figures.caption: Steep at the start, flat later. The first two anchors buy most of what any number of anchors can buy — which is the closed-form reason the two-anchor result is not luck.
figures.x_label: k — labelled anchors in the new environment

cards.question:
Write the empirical-Bayes shrinkage estimator for a new environment, and
say what its shape predicts about anchor count.
cards.reading:
A new environment's parameter is a weighted blend of its own few labels
and the population prior, with the weight rising as anchors accumulate.
cards.title: Pillar 1 — shrinkage

cards.explanation:
Only the PRODUCT is identified, which is why it is reported as one scalar
rather than two: in the swept grid r·p explains most of the variance in
recalibrated count error, with a helpful band around unity. An anchor that
miscounts devices is worse than no anchor at all — the plot's left-hand
blow-up is that statement. The conventional remedy is to import a
published conversion factor and hope it holds; the thesis rejects that
twice over, because the factor is non-stationary across crowd TYPES, and
because a point correction converts an unknown bias into a confident
number. Instead the ratio is a jointly identified latent, and its residual
uncertainty is PROPAGATED — it widens the predictive distribution rather
than shifting a point estimate.

fields.meaning: estimated number of people
observed device or identifier count
detection rate — the fraction of present devices actually seen
penetration — the fraction of people carrying a detectable device

figures.caption: The error blows up as r·p falls below one and flattens above it. The helpful band sits around unity — which is what the participant protocol is designed to occupy.

cards.question:
Write the conversion from a device count to a headcount, and say why the
thesis calls the denominator a sufficient statistic.
cards.reading:
The headcount estimate is the observed device count divided by the product
of detection rate and device-carriage penetration.
cards.title: The device-to-person conversion

cards.explanation:
The two properties are MONOTONICITY — adding a sensor never reduces
coverage — and SUBMODULARITY — the marginal gain of adding one shrinks as
the set grows. Both were measured on this problem rather than assumed:
the placement objective came out exactly monotone submodular with zero
violations across the tested pairs. The result that earns the pillar is
not the bound itself but what the framing exposes: covering the paths
people take and concentrating sensing on the busy hub are DIFFERENT
submodular objectives, so coverage-optimal and counting-optimal placements
are provably distinct and neither dominates. That turns a descriptive
blind-spot figure into a placement objective with a proof.

fields.meaning: coverage objective over a set of placed sensors
the set greedy placement produces
the optimal set of the same size
the Nemhauser–Wolsey–Fisher bound

figures.caption: The bound tightens to 1 - 1/e from above as the budget grows. For a small sensor budget the guarantee is better than the famous number.

cards.question:
State the approximation guarantee greedy sensor placement carries, and the
two properties it needs.
cards.reading:
Greedily adding the sensor with the largest marginal coverage gets you at
least about 63 per cent of the best possible set.
cards.title: Pillar 4 — the greedy guarantee

cards.explanation:
MAE stays for two reasons: comparability with a literature that reports
it, and because a distribution's mean must not be allowed to drift
unnoticed. But it is NOT sufficient, and the thesis proves that
empirically rather than stylistically. Scored on MAE alone the point and
distributional output contracts are nearly indistinguishable under
environment shift; scored on band ranked-probability score and calibration
error they are not remotely so, and it is the latter pair that tracks
whether a deployment moved to a new room can be trusted. A metric set
reporting only MAE would have CONCEALED the single clearest
cross-environment result the thesis holds.

true count for window i
number of scored windows

figures.caption: Absolute error charges a mistake in proportion to its size; squared error charges a big mistake far more. On a 0–10 count range that difference decides which estimator wins.

Write mean absolute error, and say why the thesis keeps it while insisting

cards.reading: The mean of the unsigned differences between estimated and true counts.
cards.title: Why the metric is absolute, not squared

cards.front: Why does the portfolio track TWO axes per hypothesis, and what are they?
cards.title: Portfolio shape
cards.why:
They are deliberately orthogonal. A claim can be firmly chosen and only
plausible, and a claim central to an early draft can be honestly retired
once its refutation condition fires. Collapsing the two axes into one
number is how a portfolio starts lying about itself.

cards.back:
BLE occupies 40 × 2 MHz channels in 2.4 GHz; three of them (37, 38, 39)
are dedicated advertising channels spread across the band to dodge Wi-Fi.
Advertisers broadcast short packets on all three per event; scanners hop
between them. Localization typically consumes the RSSI of these
advertisements.
cards.front: How does BLE advertising work at the radio level?
cards.title: BLE advertising

cards.back:
Invert the log-distance model: d = d0·10^((PL0 − RSSI)/(10n)). Limits:
fading makes instantaneous RSSI ±5–10 dB noisy, n is environment-
dependent, bodies/orientation shadow the signal, and TX-power/antenna
variation across devices shifts the intercept. Meter-level indoors only
with aggregation.
cards.front: How does RSSI-based ranging work and what limits it?
cards.title: RSSI ranging

cards.back:
Geometric methods invert a propagation model per anchor (no survey, but
model-error-limited indoors). Fingerprinting matches a live vector against
a surveyed radio map (captures multipath structure, so more accurate —
but the map goes stale when the environment changes: the drift problem).
cards.front: Fingerprinting vs geometric (trilateration) localization — the trade?
cards.title: Fingerprinting vs geometry

(count-without-identify) that labels CSI data without cameras or manual
counting. (2) Calibration reference: periodic BLE campaigns re-anchor the
drifting CSI→count mapping. Cheap continuous BLE monitoring triggers
expensive recalibration.

cell) + large rooms flipped the trend from +0.08 to −0.48 dB/person, made
all seeds' ρ negative, and resolved coarse steps (ΔN ≥ 4) — but fine
ΔN = 2 stayed unresolved. Design input for the hardware protocol:
concentrate anchors on hubs, not periphery.
cards.front:
Did topology-informed anchor placement recover the graded count that
dispersed placement lost?
cards.title: Placement recovery

cards.back:
BLE. In the topology campaign its location fingerprints were roughly two
and a half times more separable than CSI's per-link fingerprints.
cards.front:
For LOCATION fingerprinting, which wins — narrowband BLE RSSI at many
anchors, or wideband CSI at few links?
cards.title: BLE vs CSI fingerprints
cards.why:
Anchor count beats bandwidth for this task, which is exactly why BLE
earns its place as the calibration side-channel rather than as a rival
counting modality.

choices: When the model is geometry-mismatched — few-anchor affine re-anchoring overfits (K=3 gave 2.39×, worse than 1.48× zero-shot) and cannot fix a wrong model shape
It never fails; any anchor count helps
Only when BLE and CSI share the same band
When more than 10 anchors are used
cards.explanation:
Cross-geometry in-silico: K=3 → 2.39×, K=5 → 1.80× (both WORSE than
zero-shot 1.48×); only K=10 → 1.40× helped, and the one floor with a real
gap stayed broken. Affine re-anchoring is the wrong tool for geometry
mismatch — converges with the "switch, not fixed-gain blend" finding.
cards.question: When does affine BLE recalibration of a CSI count model FAIL?
cards.title: Affine recalibration limits

cards.back:
One Kalman filter over [count, calibration_bias]: CSI observes count+bias
every step, BLE observes count at campaigns. The fusion weight IS the
Kalman gain; the trigger IS sequential change-point detection (CUSUM) on
the cross-modal disagreement; recalibrate-now is optimal stopping.
cards.front:
In the state-space view, what do "fusion weight" and "recalibration
trigger" become?
cards.title: Kalman-style fusion

cards.back:
The cross-modal DISAGREEMENT between independently calibrated CSI→count
and BLE→count estimates tracks true error (pilot Spearman 0.93; powered
replication 0.68). CSI-only distribution monitoring (KS on features)
false-fires on 17% of error-irrelevant shifts — feature shift ≠ model
degradation.
cards.front:
Which statistic detects CSI model drift, and which plausible alternative
false-alarms?
cards.title: Drift detection statistic

choices: Parity on error at roughly one quarter of the calibration spend — condition-based maintenance, not error reduction
It beats fixed cadence on error at matched budget
It eliminates the need for calibration entirely
It halves the error at double the spend
cards.explanation:
At matched budget even a perfect-knowledge trigger did NOT beat evenly
spaced recalibration on error (0.421 vs 0.399) — scheduled recal also
fixes below-threshold drift. The payoff is parity at ~¼ the spend (2.0 vs
8.0 recals across a 4-zone estate). Never claim "event-driven beats
fixed."
cards.question:
What is the honest payoff of the drift-triggered recalibration policy vs
a fixed calendar cadence?
cards.title: Trigger economics

cards.back:
Disagreement is symmetric — it cannot tell stale-anchor from wrong-CSI. A
fresh BLE anchor can be wrongly diluted by CSI noise in a purely
condition-modulated fusion. Deployable answer: hybrid clock-GATED
freshness + condition-MODULATED staleness; log both the disagreement and
the anchor age.
cards.front:
Why can't the cross-modal disagreement statistic alone decide WHICH
modality is wrong?
cards.title: Symmetry limitation

cards.back:
CSI-based crowd counting has a mechanism that travels but a scale that
does not: a formal four-pillar theory (hierarchical calibration,
scattering saturation, state-space fusion, spectral+coverage) explains
why, predicts the empirical results already in hand, and prescribes the
BLE-calibrated architecture that keeps deployed models honest.
cards.front: State the thesis in one sentence, theory-first.
cards.title: The reframe

cards.back:
"Mechanism travels, scale doesn't" = a partial-pooling random-effects
model: a shared count→variance link with per-environment (and nested
per-platform) scale parameters. Recalibration = empirical-Bayes
shrinkage of a new environment's parameters toward the population prior;
anchor placement = Bayesian-optimal design.
cards.front: Pillar 1 (hierarchical calibration): claim and formal object?
cards.title: Pillar 1 — statement

cards.back:
(1) Slope sign-stable in 100% of environments but scale platform-
stratified: dispersion 0.96 flat → 0.28 within-platform. (2) EB shrinkage
with k = 2 anchors gives MAE 1.23 ≈ the independently measured 2-anchor
recalibration 1.32 — "42% with 2 anchors" reproduced as shrinkage, not
luck. (3) Nested prior tightens every endpoint: zero-shot 1.97 → 1.49
(beating the log-affine LOEO 1.75), k=2 → 1.13, oracle → 0.88.
cards.front: The three real-data confirmations of Pillar 1 (n = 939, 7 environments)?
cards.title: Pillar 1 — evidence

cards.back:
Model CSI as a sum of independent random phasors, one per mover; CLT
gives amplitude-variance growth that saturates: Var ≈ σ²(1 − e^(−K/K0)).
Predicts presence-easy/counting-hard AND the 5 GHz > 2.4 GHz band
ordering as wavelength effects — the empirical facts become theorems.
cards.front: Pillar 2 (scattering saturation): derivation and law?
cards.title: Pillar 2 — statement

cards.back:
(1) Concave-saturating beats linear by AIC in 5/7 counting-band
environments — WiMANS 5 GHz rooms unanimous (ΔAIC 45–95) with saturation
genuinely in-range (K0/Kmax 0.26–0.52); the 2 linear holdouts reported
honestly. (2) Band ordering 5 > 2.4 GHz by Cohen's d in 3/3 rooms (216
extra 2.4 GHz WiMANS files pulled to close the leg). One leg from
"strong": low-density Var ∝ K on first-party hardware.
cards.front: Pillar 2's two real-data confirmations?
cards.title: Pillar 2 — evidence

cards.back:
A Kalman filter over state [count, calibration_bias]: CSI measures
count + bias continuously, BLE measures count at campaigns. Fusion weight
= the Kalman gain; drift trigger = CUSUM change-point detection on
cross-modal disagreement; when-to-recalibrate = optimal stopping with a
cost knob.
cards.front:
Pillar 3 (state-space fusion): what single object unifies fusion,
trigger, and recalibration?
cards.title: Pillar 3 — statement

cards.back:
In-silico: filter MAE 0.53 vs best constant blend 0.84 vs CSI-only 1.53;
CUSUM reaches calendar parity at budget ratio 0.38 (≈¼, matching the
campaign); innovation-tracks-error ρ = 0.97 (campaign pilot 0.93).
Caveat: all synthetic-drift corpus — it stays candidate until the real
drift leg lands. Modelling lesson: trigger on raw cross-modal
disagreement with CURRENT BLE, not the whitened KF innovation.
cards.front: Pillar 3's supporting numbers, and why does it honestly stay a candidate?
cards.title: Pillar 3 — evidence and caveat

cards.back:
(4a) A STILL crowd's count is a spectral moment: amplitude variance
starves (breathing power buried under noise) but off-DC Doppler
line-counting recovers it. (4b) Sensor placement is monotone submodular
coverage maximisation — greedy achieves ≥ 1 − 1/e; counting-optimal and
coverage-optimal placements genuinely differ (Pareto front).
cards.front: Pillar 4 (spectral + coverage): the two linked claims?
cards.title: Pillar 4 — statement

cards.back:
In the STILL regime the off-DC Doppler peak-count feature clearly beats
amplitude variance, because variance starves when nobody moves. In the
MOVING regime variance already explains almost everything and the
spectral feature adds nothing. The two pillars partition by regime rather
than compete.
cards.front:
Pillar 4: how do the spectral feature and the variance feature partition
by regime, and what feature-design detail decided it?
cards.title: Pillar 4a — numbers
cards.why:
The design detail mattered: band-power SUMS drown in broadband noise.
COUNT the spectral lines instead.

choices: Parity-at-¼-budget → Pillar 2 (scattering saturation)
42% recovery with 2 anchors → Pillar 1 (EB shrinkage)
Presence easy, counting hard → Pillar 2 (concave variance law)
5 GHz > 2.4 GHz → Pillar 2 (wavelength prediction)
cards.explanation:
Parity-at-¼-budget belongs to Pillar 3 (optimal stopping / CUSUM
economics), not Pillar 2. The other three pairings are correct — knowing
which result is evidence for which pillar is exactly what a committee
probes.
cards.question:
Which empirical finding is EXPLAINED BY which pillar? Match the odd one
out.
cards.title: Cross-pillar unification

cards.back:
P1 hierarchical-calibration: chosen + supported (real n=939 fit,
promoted). P2 scattering-saturation: chosen + supported (concave 5/7 +
band 3/3 real). P3 state-space-fusion: deferred/candidate (in-silico
only — needs real drift). P4 spectral+coverage: candidate (4a selftest +
torun-adjacent; 4b design-layer). Never present P3/P4 as confirmed.
cards.front: The honest two-axis standing of the four pillars, right now?
cards.title: Honest standing

cards.back:
Mechanism: per-env ρ(count, CV) = +0.70…+1.00 in 7/7 real environments
across 2 platforms. Scale: platforms occupy separated CV bands
(meneghello ~0.4–0.5 vs WiMANS ~0.03–0.2); zero-shot LOEO MAE 1.75 vs
in-env oracle 0.72 vs predict-mean 2.07. The rank transfers; the absolute
mapping needs anchors.
cards.front:
"The mechanism travels, the scale does not" — give the concrete numbers
behind the slogan.
cards.title: What travels

cards.back:
Under repeated sampling, 95% of intervals constructed this way would
cover the true parameter. Misreading: "there is a 95% probability the
parameter is in THIS interval" — that is a credible-interval (Bayesian)
statement, not a frequentist CI.
cards.front:
What does a 95% confidence interval actually mean, and what is the
committee-bait misreading?
cards.title: Confidence intervals

cards.back:
Spearman correlates RANKS — robust to monotone nonlinearity and outliers,
right for small-n campaign reductions. But it saturates near 1 for ANY
monotone relation, so it is blind to effect MAGNITUDE — which is why the
band-ordering claim uses Cohen's d, not ρ.
cards.front:
When do we use Spearman ρ instead of Pearson r, and what is Spearman
blind to?
cards.title: Spearman vs Pearson

cards.back:
The standard equivalence test: declare equivalence iff BOTH one-sided
tests reject — the effect is significantly above −Δ AND below +Δ (i.e.
the CI falls inside the equivalence margin). Failing TOST means you
CANNOT claim equivalence; it does NOT prove a difference. The powered
drift-trigger replication failed TOST vs the oracle — so "≈ oracle" from
the pilot must not travel.
cards.front: What is TOST (two one-sided tests), and what does failing it mean?
cards.title: TOST

cards.back:
D = the maximum gap between two empirical CDFs; nonparametric test that
two samples come from one distribution. Trap: pooling links × seeds as
"observations" inflates n with non-independent points → over-powered
p-values. Cite the per-(link,seed) statistic, not the pooled one.
cards.front:
What does the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov test measure, and what
independence trap did our campaigns hit?
cards.title: KS test

cards.back:
Distribution-free finite-sample marginal coverage: calibrate the
nonconformity scores on held-out data and the resulting prediction
intervals contain the truth with probability ≥ 1−α, under exchangeability
— no Gaussian or model-correctness assumptions. Our conformal-count-
intervals hypothesis rides on the anchored/drift-weighted variant.
cards.front: What guarantee does conformal prediction give a count estimator?
cards.title: Conformal prediction

cards.back:
Nonparametric monotone-trend test on a time series (counts concordant vs
discordant pairs); no linearity or normality assumptions. Used for drift
claims: "does error trend upward over sessions" — paired with Sen's slope
for magnitude. One of the named sim_reduction_run reductions.
cards.front: Mann–Kendall test — what is it for and why do we use it?
cards.title: Mann–Kendall

cards.back:
d = (mean₁ − mean₂) / pooled SD — a standardised mean difference.
Conventionally 0.2 small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large. We report d when the
claim is about magnitude (band ordering 3/3 rooms; BLE presence
d = 2.3–3.7) and keep ρ for monotone association.
cards.front: Cohen's d — definition and the rough interpretation ladder?
cards.title: Effect sizes

cards.back:
A single seed is one draw from run-level randomness (placement, arrival,
channel noise) — its point estimate has unknown spread; T* was measured
seed-fragile ([0.25, 1.5, 0.25] m across seeds). House rule: multi-seed
runs reduced via multi_seed_ci (mean + CI over seeds); single-seed
numbers are labelled anecdotes.
cards.front:
Why does every simulation claim require multiple seeds, and what is the
house mechanism?
cards.title: Multiple seeds

choices: Session-fingerprint leakage — occupancy is confounded with session/day/channel, so the classifier identifies the recording session, not the occupancy
The features are excellent and the problem is solved
The dataset is unusually clean
AUC saturates at high n regardless of signal
cards.explanation:
persons=0/1/2 each map to distinct sessions (different days AND
channels), so file-level CV separates sessions perfectly. The mechanism
scalar showed NO 0-vs-1 difference (MWU p = 0.83). Perfect scores demand
a leakage audit before celebration.
cards.question:
The Zaman occupancy dataset gave AUC = 1.000 for EVERY feature family.
What is the correct diagnosis?
cards.title: Leakage

cards.back:
Leave-One-{Session, Room, Environment}-Out: hold out an entire group so
the test set shares no session/room/environment identity with training.
Random splits leak group fingerprints and overstate accuracy; the honest
generalisation number is the group-held-out one (our LOEO across 7 real
environments).
cards.front:
LOSO / LORO / LOEO — what are they and why do they matter more than
random splits?
cards.title: Cross-validation design

cards.back:
MI measures how much count information the feature carries independent of
any downstream model or threshold choice — comparable across sims and
datasets. OPERAnet real data: I(count; CSI-amp-variance) = 0.174 nats,
inside the sim's predicted 0.15–0.31 band; mean amplitude only 0.04.
cards.front:
Why report mutual information I(count; feature) in nats alongside
accuracy?
cards.title: Information-theoretic evaluation

cards.back:
The full Phase-4 analysis harness (4 calibration regimes, drift-slope
contrasts, LOSO/LORO, named baselines, and an explicit DEFEATER rule) was
written, self-tested, and locked BEFORE any hardware data exists — the
capture schema is defined by the analysis, so results cannot be
garden-of-forking-paths artefacts.
cards.front: What makes the IP-106 hardware protocol a genuine pre-registration?
cards.title: Pre-registration

choices: Predict-the-mean (2.07): zero-shot transfer barely beats knowing nothing, a +1.04-person penalty vs in-env oracle 0.72 — that gap IS the case for recalibration
A random classifier at 50%
Human annotator error
The state of the art from the literature
cards.explanation:
Named baselines (predict-mean, in-env oracle) bracket every reported
number in the cross-env study: 0.72 oracle < 1.32 two-anchor < 1.75
zero-shot < 2.07 predict-mean. Without the bracket, 1.75 means nothing.
cards.question: Which baseline turns "zero-shot MAE 1.75" from a number into a finding?
cards.title: Baselines

cards.back:
A hierarchical model where group parameters are drawn from a shared
prior: estimates shrink toward the population mean in proportion to their
uncertainty. Pillar 1 models per-environment calibration this way — the
measured "42% recovery with 2 anchors" is REPRODUCED as EB shrinkage
(posterior k=2 MAE 1.23 ≈ measured 1.32), so the empirical result becomes
a prediction of the theory.
cards.front:
What is partial pooling / empirical-Bayes shrinkage, and where does it
appear in the thesis?
cards.title: Partial pooling

cards.back:
Under a weak (flat) prior, extreme-spread D-optimal placement helps
(1.14 < 1.24 random); under the strong nested prior it INVERTS
(1.31 > 1.13) because it over-leverages noisy count tails. The correct
criterion is Bayesian-optimal design — maximise posterior information
GIVEN the prior. The hypothesis defeater was sharpened accordingly.
cards.front:
Frequentist D-optimal vs Bayesian-optimal anchor placement — which wins
and why?
cards.title: Optimal design

cards.back:
Coverage exhibits diminishing returns (adding a sensor helps less the
more you already have) = submodular set function; for monotone submodular
objectives greedy selection achieves ≥ (1 − 1/e) ≈ 63% of the optimum
(Nemhauser 1978). Verified 0 violations on our floor geometry; greedy hit
1.00 of optimal there. Counting-optimal ≠ coverage-optimal (Jaccard 0.50)
→ Pareto front.
cards.front:
Why does submodularity license greedy sensor placement, and with what
guarantee?
cards.title: Submodularity

cards.back:
NVIDIA's differentiable ray-tracing radio-propagation engine (part of the
Sionna link-level library): a 3D scene with material properties yields
per-path channels → CFR/CSI tensors. Our sionna-csi-runner wraps it:
scene + emitters + scatterers (agents as lossy primitives) → synthetic
CSI over time; CPU on CI, Apple Metal locally (~12× faster).
cards.front: What is Sionna RT and how do we use it?
cards.title: Sionna RT

cards.back:
walk-notebook (JuPedSim + agenda/FSM engine on a real floor bundle)
produces trajectories → sionna-csi-runner replays them as moving
scatterers over the ray-traced scene → links.parquet of per-link CSI
features + occupancy. One experiment, two physics engines, shared
geometry from PostGIS.
cards.front: Describe the coupled crowd→channel experiment chain.
cards.title: Coupled chain

choices: Structure and sensitivity evidence only — the noise model is self-authored, so sim cannot confirm its own absolute accuracy claims
Full empirical evidence, since the ray tracer solves Maxwell-accurate physics
No evidence value at all
Evidence for 2.4 GHz but not 5 GHz
cards.explanation:
The campaign-rigor audit's standing verdict: the sim corpus is
self-confirming for accuracy numbers. Sim results inform structure,
mechanisms, and sensitivity; accuracy claims need real data (OPERAnet,
WiMANS, first-party hardware).
cards.question: What epistemic status do our synthetic-CSI campaign results have?
cards.title: What sim may claim

cards.back:
OPERAnet exp028 (real Bristol capture, 6→1 people): CSI amplitude
variance steps down monotonically with count; I(count; variance) = 0.174
nats, CI [0.139, 0.208] — INSIDE the sim's predicted 0.15–0.31 band.
The sim is validated where it claims counting works, which makes its
walls-kill-counting negative a credible prediction rather than an
artefact.
cards.front: What is the one POSITIVE sim-to-real validation we hold, precisely?
cards.title: External validation

cards.back:
Synthetic 2-floor room-ID hits 0.99 vs 0.83 on real data: floor identity
is redundantly encoded (absolute level + spread + delay spread + K).
Neither feature-level impairments (even AGC σ16 dB → 0.866) nor
tensor-level CFO/STO/phase chains (→ 0.974) close the gap — no single
impairment dents it. Fix is scene/material DIVERSITY, not a post-hoc
noise knob (WiSegRT ablation predicts this).
cards.front:
What is the sim's known "over-coding" failure and why can't a noise layer
fix it?
cards.title: Over-coding

cards.back:
The absolute diffuse-power form (p_d0/γ) swamped the ray-traced channel
by ~80 dB — sim CSI became overlay-dominated and material/geometry drift
was byte-identical (inert). Fix: K_dB(N) = k0 − slope·N, with per-link
diffuse power = |H_det|²/K(N) — diffuse is now a bounded fraction of each
link's ray-traced power and inherits the scene physics.
cards.front:
Why was occupancy-diffuse power reparameterised to channel-relative
Rician K (IP-119)?
cards.title: Rician-K reparameterisation

cards.back:
Re-identification — re-fitting the drifted map against fresh anchors —
recovers most of the count-MAE penalty. Resetting to the original
calibration recovers almost none of it, at every cadence tested.
cards.front:
On the ray-traced material-drift sweep, what is the difference between
recalibration-as-RESET and recalibration-as-RE-IDENTIFICATION?
cards.title: Material drift result
cards.why:
Recalibration is not "restore the factory setting". It is a local re-fit,
and that distinction is what the whole calibration spine rests on.

cards.back:
Only when clutter intersects the link plane. Real-height furniture
(0.45–0.9 m) below a 2.4 m Tx / 1.2 m Rx plane is CSI-invisible (max
per-link Δ 0.08 dB); force footprints to 1.8 m → 9.17 dB; drop Rx to
0.6 m → 13.23 dB. Gate ≈ 100–165× either way. Bodies (1.7 m) span the
plane and own the channel; a furniture-blind CSI model is defensible in
this geometry — a furniture-blind WALKER model is not.
cards.front: When is furniture visible to CSI, per the furniture observatory?
cards.title: Furniture and the antenna plane

cards.back:
The busiest AND best-instrumented room read its own occupancy WORST
(corr −0.06; lowest amplitude variance = saturated), while a near-empty
room with one Rx read +0.53. Spearman(peak occupancy, observability)
= −0.70: busier rooms are LESS legible — dense hubs saturate under
constant occlusion. Caveat: observability was defined as LINEAR
correlation; near-zero ≠ no information.

cards.title: Observability paradox

cards.back:
Metal is ~12× faster but Float32-bound with path depth ≤ 4, and the Metal
PathSolver LOSES deep-shadow paths (~73 dB discrepancy vs llvm in deep
shadow) — fine for relative sweeps, not for absolute deep-null claims.
RadioMapSolver adds its own traps (sample cap, deterministic lattice —
fixed by rotation averaging).

criteria, budget) executed by a supervisor that fans out runs, reduces

critic, and SEALS the session (immutable, ULID-identified, vault-synced).
Experiments are campaigns — not ad-hoc scripts.

validation, not tensor-level fidelity; the impairment magnitudes (CFO
~200 Hz vs CARM's measured 80 kHz) are physically motivated but
uncalibrated.

cards.back:
The complex frequency response H(f) of the radio channel, estimated per
OFDM subcarrier (amplitude + phase per tone, per Tx-Rx antenna pair) from
the known preamble of each received frame. It describes how the environment
transformed the transmitted signal.
cards.front: What is Channel State Information (CSI) in Wi-Fi?
cards.title: What CSI is
cards.why: The opening definition — say it in one breath.

cards.back:
RSSI is one scalar per frame (total received power). CSI resolves the
channel per subcarrier and per antenna pair, so it preserves frequency
selectivity and phase — small path changes reshape the CSI pattern even
when total power (RSSI) barely moves.
cards.front: Why is CSI a richer sensing observable than RSSI?
cards.title: CSI vs RSSI

cards.back:
Indoors the signal arrives as a sum of paths (direct, reflected,
scattered). A body blocks, reflects, and scatters individual paths;
because CSI resolves the channel finely, these per-path perturbations
shift the amplitude/phase pattern measurably.
cards.front: Why does indoor multipath make CSI sensitive to human presence?
cards.title: Multipath
cards.why: The first-principles opener a committee uses to test depth vs. recitation.

cards.back:
Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiplexing splits the band into many
narrow orthogonal subcarriers. Equalising them requires estimating the
per-subcarrier channel from known pilots/preamble — that estimate IS the
CSI; sensing reuses what communication must compute anyway.
cards.front: What is OFDM and why does it give us CSI "for free"?
cards.title: OFDM

cards.back:
Rayleigh: no dominant path, the channel is a sum of many comparable
scattered components (magnitude Rayleigh-distributed). Rician: one
dominant (usually LoS) path plus diffuse scatter; the K-factor is the
ratio of dominant to diffuse power. K → 0 recovers Rayleigh.
cards.front: Rayleigh vs Rician fading — when does each apply?
cards.title: Fading models

cards.back:
K = deterministic (dominant-path) power / diffuse (scattered) power.
People add scatterers and block dominant paths, so K tends to fall as
occupancy rises — the diffuse fraction of the channel is where the crowd
signature lives.
cards.front:
What does the Rician K-factor measure, and why does it matter for crowd
sensing?
cards.title: Rician K

cards.back:
Motion changes path lengths over time; each moving scatterer modulates the
channel at a rate set by its radial velocity relative to the path
geometry. Indoor human motion lives at low Doppler frequencies — well
under ~300 Hz at Wi-Fi bands (CARM); walking is tens of Hz.
cards.front:
What creates the Doppler signature in Wi-Fi sensing, and roughly where
does indoor human motion sit spectrally?
cards.title: Doppler

cards.back:
v_max = λ · PRR / 4 — the packet-rate PRR bounds the fastest motion whose
Doppler you can sample unaliased (λ ≈ 5.6 cm at 5.3 GHz). Reported by
Ropitault et al. 2024 and Wang et al. 2022 — NOT by the qualitative-Doppler
papers (ma2020, chen2023, du2025).
cards.front:
What is the maximum trackable speed relation for CSI packet-rate sensing,
and who reports it?
cards.title: Speed–sampling relation
cards.why: Known citation trap — the formula is real, the usual citation is wrong.

cards.back:
PL(d) = PL(d0) + 10·n·log10(d/d0) + X, with path-loss exponent n (~2 free
space, 2–4+ indoors) and shadowing term X. It predicts mean received power
vs distance; fading rides on top of it.
cards.front: What is the log-distance path-loss model?
cards.title: Path loss

cards.back:
Coherence time: how long the channel stays effectively constant (set by
Doppler spread) — bounds the useful sampling interval. Coherence
bandwidth: over what frequency span the channel is flat (set by delay
spread) — determines how many independent subcarrier looks you get.
cards.front:
Coherence time and coherence bandwidth — what do they tell a sensing
system designer?
cards.title: Coherence

cards.explanation:
HT20 uses 56 usable tones (52 data + 4 pilots) out of a 64-point FFT;
legacy (a/g) OFDM uses 52; 242 is the 20 MHz resource-unit tone count in
802.11ax (HE). Our AX210 fleet observes 52- and 56-tone frames interleaved
on an ambient channel.
cards.question:
A 20 MHz 802.11n (HT) transmission delivers CSI on how many usable
subcarriers?
cards.title: Subcarrier counts

choices: Shorter wavelength: each mover perturbs the phasor sum by a larger fraction of λ, so per-mover fluctuation magnitude is larger
5 GHz has more subcarriers, so more information is always captured
2.4 GHz is absorbed by water and people are mostly water
5 GHz propagates further indoors, illuminating more of the room
cards.explanation:
The scattering-saturation pillar treats the band ordering as a wavelength
prediction about fluctuation magnitude per mover — confirmed on WiMANS by
Cohen's d in 3/3 rooms (measure magnitude with d, not Spearman ρ, which
saturates for any monotone relation).
cards.question:

cards.back:
The power-weighted spread of path arrival times from the channel impulse
response. Practical traps: window the CFR (e.g. Hann) before the IFFT or
sinc sidelobes read as fake multipath, and threshold taps (~−20 dB) or you
measure the noise floor.
cards.front: What is RMS delay spread and what practical trap does measuring it hide?
cards.title: Delay spread

cards.back:
The first body changes the channel a lot (large marginal effect); each
additional body adds a diminishing perturbation as the diffuse field
saturates. Our scattering law derives this: variance grows concavely with
count, Var ≈ σ²(1 − e^(−K/K0)), so the count signal compresses at high
occupancy.
cards.front: Why is detecting presence easy but counting hard in CSI sensing?
cards.title: Presence vs counting

cards.back:

scheduling, and CSI-style feedback so sensing no longer depends on
vendor-specific CSI extraction hacks. Relevant as the "this will be
mainstream" framing for the thesis motivation.

cards.title: Sensing standardisation

cards.back:
Raw per-packet phase is scrambled by CFO/SFO offsets (uniform-random
intercepts). Dividing CSI of two RX chains on the same NIC cancels the
common oscillator terms. Measured on our AX210 link: raw phase intercept
std 3.5 rad → ratio phase circular std 0.26 rad; amplitude CV 0.32 → 0.20.
Two active RX chains are therefore a hard capture requirement.

The pair (ntone, modulation) of a CSI record. An ambient channel
interleaves unlike frames packet-by-packet (measured: 74% legacy-52 +
26% HT-56 on ch11), so mixing classes compares incompatible tone grids.
Every csiscope/IP-121 analytical view is scoped to one class.

analytical view scope to one?

cards.back:

reading real-first yields i·conj(H) — amplitudes unchanged, every phase
mirrored. Decided by CIR causality: correct order gives early/late tap
energy ratio 21.3; swapped gives 0.48 (anti-causal, impossible).

cards.back:
Ambient/hostapd multicast is bursty (no ACK/retry; DTIM/queue bunching:
gap p50 15 ms vs commanded 40 ms, CV 2.6, 12% of wall time in >1 s
stalls) — inter-arrival is Erlang-like, not a clean sampling clock. Answer:
a paced monitor-mode injector in csid (absolute-deadline pacing, missed
slots skipped) or a unicast stream.
cards.front:
Why does passive ambient traffic fail as a Doppler-grade sampling source,
and what is our answer?
cards.title: Illuminator

choices: Source MAC sentinel ef:be:ad:de:ad:de (driver-side 0xdeadbeef fill)
By the AP's real MAC address
By a custom vendor IE in the beacon
By their fixed 56-tone HT format
cards.explanation:
Broadcast data frames without a station context get the deadbeef fill
pattern as smac; the AP's real MAC appears only on beacons. Filter on the
sentinel, not the AP MAC. (They are 52-tone legacy frames, not HT-56.)
cards.question: How are our illuminator frames identified in captures?
cards.title: Sentinel MAC

cards.back:
(1) The reported value is a positive magnitude — the dBm value is its
negative (valid range −18..−89 dBm). (2) −127 dBm is a firmware
"no measurement" sentinel, and that chain's CSI block is then a stale
duplicate (exact biconditional over 44k records). (3) Ambient vs
illuminated frames make RSSI bimodal — scope by source MAC.
cards.front: Three iax/AX210 RSSI facts every analysis must respect?
cards.title: RSSI semantics

cards.back:
Above roughly 80 °C the Pi 5 firmware throttles the ARM clock while
cpufreq keeps reporting the nominal frequency. The only truth is
`get_throttled` — its live bits and its sticky bits.
cards.front:
A fanless fleet node reports a healthy performance governor at 2.4 GHz.
Why is that not evidence it is running at full speed?
cards.title: Fleet thermals
cards.why:
The hottest fanless node idles in the low eighties, a few degrees under
the hard limit, so this is not a hypothetical. A node that looks healthy
in every governor reading can be silently cooked, and the fan is what
splits the fleet into two thermal populations.

cards.back:
No. The proof-of-concept benchmark sustained 2x2 HE CSI at several
hundred hertz — an order of magnitude above the paces the experiments
use.
cards.front:
Is the experiment's packet pace a hardware limit on the Pi 5 + AX210
stack?
cards.title: Capture ceiling
cards.why:
Pacing is therefore an experimental-design choice, not a ceiling. Saying
"the hardware could not go faster" would be false, and the rate ladder
later confirmed the pacer holds to 500 Hz with zero transmit errors.

cards.back:
CSI delivery is unicast by driver design: userspace registers by sending
the CSI vendor subcommand, and the driver stores that socket's portid and
targets events to it alone. Registration must come from the same netlink
socket that receives — hence a single daemon (csid) owns the stream and
fans out via a local socket.
cards.front: Why can only ONE process per node consume AX210 CSI events?
cards.title: One consumer

cards.back:
The iax backport firmware asserts (FW error in LINK_CONFIG_CMD) when the
AX210 brings up a 5 GHz AP — not a regulatory issue. Workarounds: 2.4 GHz
hostapd arms, campus-AP traffic for 5 GHz arms, or the csid injector
(monitor-mode, no AP path — works on 5 GHz).
cards.front:
What blocks 5 GHz hostapd illumination on the fleet, and what is the
workaround?
cards.title: 5 GHz AP crash

choices: Antenna count — the +30–40% gain came from joint 4-antenna 802.11ax + finer subcarrier spacing; widening 20→160 MHz alone was marginal
Bandwidth — 160 MHz resolves multipath the antennas cannot
Transmit power — SNR dominates everything
Carrier frequency — 6 GHz is strictly better
cards.explanation:
The +30–40% figure is the JOINT 4-antenna-11ax + finer-spacing move, not
antennas alone — a precision worth having exactly right when citing it.
Design consequence: sweep the antenna knob, not bandwidth, in simulation.
cards.question:
For sensing discriminability, which hardware knob matters more according
to Cominelli et al. 2023?
cards.title: Antennas vs bandwidth

cards.back:
Quasi-static night blocks separated by discrete state jumps — drift is
not a smooth ramp but plateaus punctuated by rearrangement events. First
first-party drift phenomenology; motivates event-detecting triggers over
fixed-rate assumptions.
cards.front:
What did the first 19-hour overnight ambient capture show about
environmental drift?
cards.title: Drift phenomenology

cards.back:
The competing channel fill. On the rate ladder, 250 Hz commanded against
a quiet channel delivered better than 50 Hz commanded against a busy one,
and the fleet spread widened from under a point to tens of points as the
fill rose.
cards.front:
What governs the delivered fraction of a paced probe — the commanded
rate, or something else?
cards.title: Delivery numbers
cards.why:
Two consequences. Two arms captured at different times are not comparable
on delivery, so channel fill is logged as a covariate for every analysis
window. And a rate that "failed" may only have met a busy channel.

decks.intro:
This chapter answers RQ1, and it has to survive a hostile reading of its own
title. The thesis is named after periodic BLE calibration, and the deployment
has never captured a real Bluetooth observation. That is stated plainly in the
implementation chapter and it is why this chapter's most important move is a
generalisation: BLE is one INSTANCE of a device-count channel, not the
category. Ambient device activity is a second instance, it costs no hardware,
and it is already recorded in every session the project has ever taken.
decks.title: Chapters · 6 BLE and Device-Activity Augmentation

decks.intro:
The conclusion is the chapter a committee reads twice: once at the start, to
find out what is being claimed, and once at the end, to check whether the
document delivered it. It is therefore the only chapter worth being able to
recite structurally rather than in fragments.
decks.title: Chapters · 11 Conclusion

decks.intro:
This is the chapter that reports a refutation, and it is the one a committee
will most enjoy. It builds the case for a physics prior carefully — three model
tiers, the conservation law, the closure that makes it solvable, the
physics-informed learning literature where the same construction demonstrably
works — and then kills it with a single well-designed ablation.
decks.title: Chapters · 7 Indoor Crowd Modelling

decks.intro:
This is the chapter that answers RQ2, and it is the longest for a reason: it
has to go from the physical layer to a defensible generalisation claim without
skipping the awkward middle. Four movements.
decks.title: Chapters · 5 CSI-Based Sensing

decks.intro:
The evaluation chapter was restructured on the day of this draft into three
evidence tiers, ordered by how much of the architecture each can test today.
Tier one delivers the cross-environment calibration results on public corpora.
Tier two delivers the instrument bounds. Tier three is the pre-registered
in-vivo campaign, whose protocol and thresholds are frozen and whose result
slots are labelled and empty.
decks.title: Chapters · 10 Evaluation

decks.intro:
The fusion chapter is where two heuristics turn out to be one object. The
thesis developed them separately and for different reasons: a staleness-weighted
switch that decides how much to trust an ageing anchor, and a disagreement
statistic that decides when to spend a new one. Treat the crowd count and the
slowly-drifting calibration as a latent state, and both fall out of a single
recursive Bayesian filter. Fusion is the filter's gain. The trigger is a
sequential change-point rule on its innovation.
decks.title: Chapters · 8 Calibration and Fusion

decks.intro:
Note the title. Not "Implementation" — "The Measurement Instrument". The
chapter's claim is that a synchronous multi-receiver array makes quantities
measurable that the field's methodology currently assumes, and that delivery,
loss and channel occupancy are measurands of a sensing instrument rather than
deployment plumbing.
decks.title: Chapters · 9 The Measurement Instrument

decks.intro:
The introduction has one job that the rest of the thesis depends on: it has to
make the problem sound difficult for the right reasons. Not "nobody has tried
this" — plenty have — but "every family that has tried it pays a price nobody
wants to pay." Privacy for cameras, cost for thermal, cooperation for
device-based tracking. The argument is a process of elimination that ends
somewhere specific: a passive, infrastructure-reusing, physics-grounded
modality.
decks.title: Chapters · 1 Introduction

decks.intro:
This is the chapter a committee will attack, because it is the one that makes
promises. It states, before any system is built, what the thesis intends to
answer and how it would know if it were wrong. Every hypothesis ships with an
explicit refutation condition and is maintained as a version-controlled note
revised as evidence accumulates.
decks.title: Chapters · 3 Objectives, Hypotheses and the Output Contract

decks.intro:
A literature chapter is judged on whether it organises or merely lists. This
one organises twice. It gives the CSI sensing field a four-axis taxonomy —
signal extraction, learning paradigm, deployment topology, target granularity
— and shows the axes are largely independent, so a system's position is a
combination rather than a category. Then it narrows to crowd counting and does
something braver: it tabulates the representative systems and admits the table
cannot be read as a league table, because MAE, discrete occupancy accuracy and
counting-plus-latency scores are not commensurable.
decks.title: Chapters · 2 State of the Art

decks.intro:
The design chapter has to survive a specific kind of question: not "does it
work" but "why is it shaped like that". Four tiers, mutually dependent yet
operationally separable, and the separation between the calibration regime and
the inference regime is the load-bearing part rather than an organisational
convenience.
decks.title: Chapters · 4 System Design

decks.intro:
Rewritten 2026-08-24 after a curation pass found the first version useless. It
gave the expansion, then a sentence about where the term sits in this thesis's
own architecture — which is backwards. "BLE stands for Bluetooth Low Energy,
and it is the calibration partner in the title" tells you nothing about what BLE
*is*. You cannot defend a term you can only place.
decks.title: Fundamentals · Abbreviations

decks.intro:
Two halves. The first is the notation table from the supporting appendix: the
mathematical symbols the thesis uses recurrently and defines once. Density and
flow symbols follow the continuum pedestrian-dynamics convention; channel
symbols follow the CSI literature. Where the two traditions collide — and they
do, on N — the thesis picks one meaning and holds it.
decks.title: Fundamentals · Definitions and symbols

decks.intro:
In July 2026 the thesis was read cold and the verdict was uncomfortable: a
competent measurement study with childish mathematics. Numbers everywhere, no
theory holding them. The four pillars were the answer, and this deck is what
the pillars reduce to — the dozen equations that carry the whole apparatus.
decks.title: Fundamentals · The formulas

decks.intro:
A defense rehearsal that drills a paraphrase of a research question is worse
than one that drills nothing, because it teaches you to answer a question the
document does not ask. So these cards are not written — they are rendered from
the same declaration the thesis itself renders from. If a question changes in
`Foundation.md`, it changes here, and nowhere is there a second copy to drift.
decks.title: Fundamentals · The research questions

decks.intro:
The commonest defense failure is not a wrong answer. It is a right answer given
from the wrong chapter — reaching for the evaluation numbers when the question
was about the architecture, or defending the instrument when the question was
about the corpus. A committee reads that as a document you have written rather
than a document you have organised.
decks.title: Fundamentals · Topics: what lives where

decks.intro:
Watch people leave a lecture hall and you will see physics: flow through the
door saturates, a queue crystallises, walking speed collapses as density
rises. Pedestrian dynamics is the discipline that made those observations
quantitative — measured on real crowds, in units of persons per square metre
— and it matters here for a simple reason: our synthetic CSI experiments are
only as credible as the crowds that generate them. If the simulated people
move wrongly, every downstream channel measurement inherits the lie. So this
track is about the walking layer: the models, the handful of parameters that
are actually grounded in literature, and the discipline of not tuning them
until an experiment happens to pass.
decks.title: CRD503 · Crowd dynamics and pedestrian simulation

decks.intro:
Committees are not adversaries; they are professionals with forty minutes to
decide whether you own your work. Their big questions are predictable in
form — summarise it, defend its worth, name its weakness, tell us what is
genuinely new — and unpredictable only in phrasing. The winning shape for an
answer is nearly always the same: concede what must be conceded in the first
sentence, then show that the concession was already priced in. "The biggest
threat is X, which is why the design includes Y" reads as command; a
defensive "well, actually" reads as fragility. The model answers here are
not scripts to memorise. Read them for their skeletons — claim, evidence,
honest limit, next step — then practise saying each one in your own words,
shorter every time.
decks.title: Defense · The big committee questions

decks.intro:
The most dangerous errors in a defense are the ones you brought yourself: a
number quoted from memory of a summary of a paper, drifted three retellings
from the source. We know exactly what these look like because a 2026 audit
of our own vault caught several — a decay figure attributed to the wrong
paper and the wrong metric, our own re-analysis numbers credited to the
dataset's authors, a formula cited to papers that never derived it. All were
fixed at source; here they are preserved deliberately, as sparring partners.
Each question below offers the seductive wrong version alongside the
audited truth. If you can feel WHY the wrong option is tempting, you are
inoculated; if you merely know the right answer, the temptation returns
under pressure.
decks.title: Defense · Committee traps and near-miss claims

decks.intro:
Formal methods have a reputation for living far from real systems, but in
this project they do manual labour. State machines drive every simulated
occupant's day; typed schemas reject malformed experiments before a single
CPU-hour is burned; a Petri net models a message pipeline in the Hermod
paper. The through-line of this short track is that a formal model is a
contract you can be held to — it makes wrong states unrepresentable and
wrong claims checkable. That mindset, more than any particular logic, is
what transfers: the same instinct that adds a timeout guard to a looping
state machine also adds a defeater clause to a hypothesis.
decks.title: FM505 · Formal modelling and verification

decks.intro:
Right now your phone is shouting into the void several times a second. BLE
advertisements — tiny broadcast packets on three channels wedged between
Wi-Fi's territory — power everything from AirTags to COVID exposure apps,
and they leak a physical quantity for free: received signal strength. It is
a crude quantity, single-number, fading-battered. But crude, cheap, and
everywhere beats precise, expensive, and absent — which is exactly the role
BLE plays in this thesis. Not the star sensor, but the honest witness: the
side-channel that tells a drifting CSI model what the ground truth roughly
is, and does so with radios the building already owns.
decks.title: LOC502 · BLE and RF localization

decks.intro:
If the defense has a home turf for the committee, it is statistics. Nobody
will re-derive your ray tracer on a whiteboard, but anyone can ask what your
confidence interval means or why you trusted a p-value at n=3. This track
collects the methods the thesis actually leans on — not statistics in
general, but the specific tools wired into the campaign reductions, each
with the scar that taught us to use it: the pilot correlation that shrank
under replication, the dataset that scored perfectly for the wrong reason,
the significant p-value that arrived exactly when the effect got smaller.
The theme throughout: effect sizes with intervals over verdicts, named
baselines over naked numbers, and pre-registration over hindsight.
decks.title: PRB504 · Probabilistic and statistical methods

decks.intro:
Why simulate at all? Because some experiments are unaffordable, unethical, or
simply impossible: you cannot rearrange a building's walls fifty times, or
hire thirty people to walk identical evenings for twenty random seeds. A
ray-traced radio channel coupled to a simulated crowd buys those experiments
for the price of CPU time. The danger is equally plain — a simulator is a
theory wearing an execution engine, and it will happily confirm the
assumptions you fed it. So this track carries both halves: the machinery
(what the toolchain actually computes) and the epistemics (which claims
survived contact with real data, which failed, and what each failure taught
us about the machine).
decks.title: SIM507 · Simulation toolkits and sim-to-real discipline

decks.intro:
In July 2026 the thesis changed shape. Reading the progress deck cold, the
verdict was uncomfortable: a competent measurement study with childish
mathematics — numbers everywhere, no theory holding them. The response was
not to measure more but to ask what single formal structure would make the
existing results inevitable. The answer became four pillars: a hierarchical
calibration model, a derived scattering law, a state-space view of fusion,
and a spectral-plus-coverage layer. Each pillar takes results that were
already in hand and re-derives them as predictions — the difference between
"we observed 42% recovery" and "the model says two anchors must recover
about this much, and they do." This deck is that theoretical core, pillar by
pillar, with its evidence and its honest gaps.
decks.title: Thesis · The four-pillar theoretical core

decks.intro:
A thesis is usually presented as a single claim. Managed honestly, it is a
portfolio of bets at different odds — and this one keeps the ledger in the
open: twenty living hypotheses, each with a machine-readable state, a
confidence score, a novelty score against named prior art, and a
pre-declared gate that would promote or kill it. The portfolio view changes
how you defend. You stop protecting weak claims (the ledger already marks
them plausible, not proven) and you stop underselling strong ones. And when
a committee member finds the refuted entries, they find evidence of a
falsification machine that actually fires — which is worth more than another
confirmation. These cards walk the bets that matter, from the anchor premise
to the flagship gamble.
decks.title: Thesis · The living-hypothesis portfolio

decks.intro:
Between the physics and the science sits a layer nobody thanks you for:
getting honest bits out of commodity silicon. Wi-Fi chips were never meant to
export their channel estimates, so every CSI dataset in the literature rests
on some half-documented vendor path — and on the assumption that the bytes
mean what the README says. Our fleet taught us how dangerous that assumption
is: two silent data-corruption bugs sat in the capture stack, invisible in
amplitude plots, poisoning every phase analysis. This deck is the
instrument-builder's view of the thesis — what the hardware actually does,
which numbers you measured yourself, and why "verify your own pipeline"
became a design principle rather than a slogan.
decks.title: WS501 · CSI extraction, hardware, and the AX210 fleet

decks.intro:
Every Wi-Fi router is an unpaid physicist. Twenty times a second it solves a
scattering problem — how did the room transform my signal? — because it must,
to decode the next frame. For thirty years that answer was computed, used, and
thrown away. This track is about keeping it. The channel estimate a router
discards is a measurement of the space between antennas: the walls, the
furniture, and crucially the people. Before any claim about counting crowds
can make sense, you need to feel why a room full of people IS a different
radio channel than an empty one. That is what these first cards build, from
the physics up.
decks.title: WS501 · The wireless channel, from first principles
